paper.title: Avoiding exp($k^*$) Scaling for Thompson Sampling in Combinatorial Semi-Bandits: From Multiple Seeds to a Single Seed

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial semi-bandits (CMAB) with general monotone, bounded-smooth reward and Gaussian base-arm outcomes
unmapped: Base-arm outcomes Z_i(t) ~ N(mu_i, 1) with arbitrary contemporaneous correlation across arms within a round
Expected reward r(S, mu) depends only on means of arms in S (Assumption 2.1), is monotone (Assumption 2.5) and 1-norm bounded smooth with constant B (Assumption 2.3)
The learner knows the reward function r and has an exact argmax oracle ORACLE(theta) (Assumption 2.8)
settings.definition_quote: At each round t, each base arm i has marginal outcome Zi(t) ∼ N(µi, 1), and the marginal outcome process of each arm is independent over time conditional on the past. ... we do not require the coordinates of Z(t) to be independent within the same round ... we consider the semi-bandit feedback, i.e., Q(t) = {(i, Zi(t)) : i ∈ S(t)}.

algorithms.name: Combinatorial Thompson Sampling with a Single Seed (CTS3)

symbols.k_star: size of the optimal super arm k^*
symbols.P_log: unspecified polynomial of log(T, d, Delta_max/Delta_min)

conditions: Assumption 2.1: expected reward depends only on means of arms in S
Assumption 2.3: 1-norm bounded smoothness with constant B
Assumption 2.5: reward monotone in the means

source.quote: Assume that Assumptions 2.1, 2.3, 2.5, and 2.8 hold. Then the regret of CTS3 satisfies E[R_I(T)] ≤ 2m∆max + O( mkk^*B^2/∆min poly(log(T, m, ∆max/∆min)) ). (4.4)

results.notes: Paper's m (number of base arms) mapped to canonical d; paper's k (largest super-arm size) mapped to canonical m. Regret defined through r(S*,mu)-r(S(t),mu), so pseudo-regret. Algorithm does not take T as input (anytime); polynomial time assuming the exact oracle. Polylog factor unspecified power, kept as symbol.

Existence of a combinatorial semi-bandit instance on which CTS incurs exponential regret in k*
